title: How much does AEO cost? Pricing by agency, tools, and software
content:
How much does AEO cost? The short answer is roughly $30 a month for a monitoring tool you run yourself to over $15,000 a month for a full-service agency program that handles everything for you — with a wide middle in between.
What lands you at one end of that range or the other is how much of the work you’re actually paying for. AEO pricing goes up with scope. A tool that only monitors your visibility in AI answers sits at the low end, while strategy, content production, and off-site authority building push the number up, and buying all of it as a managed service sits at the top.
This guide breaks down AEO cost by approach, by budget tier, and by what a realistic pilot should run, so you can size the spend against what your team needs.
AEO cost spans a wide range, from monitoring tools that start in the low tens of dollars a month (such as HubSpot AEO at $50/mo) to full-service agency programs at thousands of dollars a month (such as RevenueZen ’s $15,000 Total Market package). Agency services can cost even more for custom packages. Where you land depends on how much of the work you’re buying, from simply tracking your visibility in AI answers to producing optimized content and building off-site authority.
AEO is just one line inside a larger AI budget, so it helps to know what AI costs across model types and tools before you size the AEO portion.
Most teams weighing the cost of AEO are choosing among three approaches:
Here’s how the three AEO options compare on price, billing, and what you typically get.
One-time audit or sprint from ~$3,000; ongoing programs ~$9,000–$15,000+
Monthly retainer, sometimes with a one-time audit or setup fee, or a hybrid retainer-plus-performance model
Strategy, content production, schema and technical work, off-site authority building, monitoring, and reporting, all managed for you
Teams that want the work executed for them and have budget for a managed program
~ $29– $489/mo for standard self-serve tiers, metered by prompts and engines covered; enterprise plans are custom
Monthly or annual subscription, usually tiered by the number of prompts tracked and engines covered
Automated tracking of how your brand appears in AI answers, share of voice against competitors, citation analysis, and recommendations you act on yourself. Anchors: HubSpot AEO at $50/mo (3 engines), Profound from $99/mo (Starter tracks ChatGPT only; multi-engine starts at the $399/mo Growth plan), Peec AI from $95/mo
Teams that want to measure and act in-house without agency fees
Tool subscription (see above) plus your team's time
You run monitoring, content, and technical work yourself with a tool rather than a retainer. With HubSpot, AEO is included in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise or available on its own without another HubSpot subscription.
Teams with in-house content and technical resources that want to control scope and cost
The spread between the low and high ends comes down to scope rather than vendor markup, which the next section breaks down.
The gap between the low and high ends of those ranges comes down to how much of the work you’re buying and how large your content library is. Five factors drive most of the spread:
These drivers explain the range. How you pay for them (by retainer, subscription, or a mix) is the next question.
AEO help is sold in four main ways, and the label on the invoice tells you a lot about what you actually get. It’s easier to compare quotes once you understand the different pricing models.
Those models map onto three rough spend tiers. What separates them is how much of the content, off-site, and reporting work from the sections above you’re paying someone else to do.
Whatever tier you choose, AEO spend works best alongside SEO rather than instead of it. That’s why it helps to know how much to budget for SEO , too.
Before you shift budget toward AEO, understand what the two disciplines share and where they split, because their budgets are related but not interchangeable.
SEO and AEO run on the same foundation: clear, credible content on a technically sound site. They diverge on where that content surfaces and how you measure it. SEO works to rank your pages in search results and earn clicks, measured by rankings, click-through rate, and impressions. AEO works to get your brand cited inside AI-generated answers, measured by mentions, share of voice, and citations. SEO also writes for a person skimming links; AEO has to satisfy the engine building the answer before any person reads it.
AEO complements SEO by improving your brand’s visibility in AI answers rather than replacing traditional search optimization. The two reinforce each other: Pages with strong Google rankings tend to get picked up as citations in AI answers (though it’s not a guarantee). Cutting SEO to fund AEO can weaken the rankings that feed those citations.
You need both because buyers use both. AI referral traffic has roughly tripled from January 2025 to December 2025, according to Search Engine Land ’s research, but still represents less than 2% of referral traffic in the study’s dataset. That overlap is also why some vendors sell ordinary SEO as AEO, which is one of the pricing red flags worth spotting before you sign anything.
The category is new enough that pricing and promises aren’t standardized, so a few patterns should make you slow down before you sign.
Once you can screen out the noise, the useful question is what a small, honest first engagement should cost.
A pilot exists to answer one question: Does AEO move anything for your brand before you commit real budget? Running one is essential for building a business case for AEO with your stakeholders. Keep the scope small enough to run in 60 to 90 days and honest enough to trust the result.
Start lean, not broad. Anchor the pilot on the lean tier from the sections above: a monitoring subscription in the low-tens-to-$50 range, optionally paired with a one-time diagnostic audit. Skip content production and off-site authority building for now. Both are ongoing, slow-moving investments, and a two-to-three-month window won’t fairly test either.
Measure what AEO is actually measured on. Use these core metrics: brand mentions, share of voice against competitors, and citations. Set your baseline in week one. Then compare against it at day 60 and day 90. Track the trend, not a single snapshot, because answer-engine results vary run to run.
Budget tip for small teams: A free trial lets you validate before you spend. HubSpot AEO offers a 28-day free trial that tracks 25 prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with no credit card, which can cover most of a short pilot’s monitoring at no cost. HubSpot AEO gives you the full picture of your AI visibility, including brand mentions and citations.
At just $50/month (or $45/month billed annually), running a comprehensive, three-month optimization pilot costs only $100 out-of-pocket — giving you a complete, continuous picture of your brand mentions and citation trends without the enterprise price tag.
If the pilot goes well, fold AEO into your recurring SEO budget planning rather than running it as a permanent side experiment.
Once a pilot proves AEO is worth scaling, the recurring question is measurement: How do you track visibility, spot where competitors get cited instead of your brand, and ultimately connect AI visibility to marketing ROI?
That’s the gap a software-led approach fills. HubSpot AEO tracks your brand’s visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity and flags where competitors win citations you’re missing. It also analyzes which domains and content types answer engines cite in your category, then returns a prioritized list of recommendations to act on. That measurement-first approach is the same one HubSpot used internally. The team documented its full three-pillar rollout, and the results, in a CRM AI-search case study .
HubSpot AEO is available on its own, without another HubSpot subscription, at $50 a month, covering visibility tracking, citation analysis, competitor benchmarking, and recommendations. If you already run Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise , AEO is included at no extra cost and connects those recommendations to your CRM data and content tools.
Yes. SEO ranks your pages in search results; AEO gets your brand cited inside AI answers. They share a foundation of credible, structured content, so most teams need both. Pages that rank well in Google often become the citations that answer engines pull from, and cutting one usually weakens the other.
Partly. A monitoring tool shows where your brand appears in AI answers and flags gaps, but it doesn’t execute the fixes. Your team still handles content, schema, and off-site work. Tools like HubSpot AEO analyze citations and surface prioritized recommendations, but you’ll need to either act on them in-house or outsource to an agency.
Expect early signals, not certainty, in the first 60 to 90 days. A focused pilot can show movement in visibility and share of voice, but content and off-site work compound slowly. Because answer engines are non-deterministic, they can give different answers to the same prompts, so track the trend rather than any single snapshot.
A clear SOW names deliverables rather than promising “full optimization.” Look for how many prompts get tracked and which engines, how many pages get produced or reworked, schema and entity work, any off-site scope, and reporting cadence. Some agencies require a three-month minimum, so confirm the term length before signing.
Start lean. Monitoring subscriptions start in the low tens to $50 range. You can also add a one-time audit. Skip high-volume content and off-site work until you have signals that your AEO efforts are working. Set a baseline, then fix cheap, high-value gaps first. HubSpot AEO offers a 28-day free trial tracking 25 prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with no credit card required.
